_comment: Canonical event facts. Hand-edited. Everything on the site reads from here — change a date or a link once, and it updates everywhere.
name: Energy Planning Week 2026

hosts.name: GET.transform
hosts.description: A technical assistance programme implemented by GIZ and co-funded by the European Union, Germany, Norway, the Netherlands, Sweden and Austria.
hosts._descriptionNote: Standard description requested by GET.transform (Sept 2026) and live on the IRENA event page. Use verbatim; do not revert to the 'several European governments' phrasing.

dates._datesNote: 1–4 December 2026 is confirmed. Earlier drafts saying 1–3 December or "three days" are superseded.

venue.name: GIZ Campus
venue.capacityNote: Up to 120 places on site. Registration is an expression of interest, not a confirmed place; on-site places are confirmed by the co-hosts. Priority is given to speakers, government planners, and members and partners of the LTES Network, GCEP and GET.transform.

format.note: Sessions run on-site in Bonn and stream online. All times are CET.

status._phaseNote: The site derives its phase from the programme dates: the opening date before the event, a live now/next strip during it, a closing message after. Nothing to set here.
status.banner: Provisional programme. Sessions, speakers and timings are subject to change until the final agenda is published.

registration.label: Register your interest
registration.note: Registration is an expression of interest, not a confirmed place.

join._urlNote: Paste the Teams event link here when it exists. Until it is set, the join buttons show as 'link coming soon' rather than dead links. GDPR: EU-hosted platforms only — no Zoom.
join.label: Join online

components.name: 7th International Forum on Long-Term Energy Scenarios
components.summary: The seventh edition of IRENA's International Forum on Long-Term Energy Scenarios, convened through the LTES Network. Government planners and scenario practitioners work through the priorities the Network identified for 2026: scenario governance and capacity, data stewardship, energy security and flexibility, climate risks, and new modelling methods.

components.name: GCEP Planning–Investment Dialogue
components.summary: Convened under the Global Coalition for Energy Planning. It puts planners in the room with financiers, regulators and utilities to work on the gap between an approved plan and an investable one — what signals finance needs from planning systems, and which bottlenecks recur across the GCEP regional dialogues.

components.name: Implementation Lab: From Plans to Delivery
components.summary: Convened by IRENA and GET.transform. It follows the plan into delivery — how planning can support enabling energy markets, from policy, regulation and procurement to market design and investment decisions — with country cases on where planning meets the market.

components.name: Partner-hosted sessions
components.summary: A day of sessions hosted by partner institutions, giving partners space to convene discussions with country teams on planning and implementation cases. Open to members and partners of GCEP, the LTES Network and GET.transform. Agenda to be confirmed.

narrative._comment: The four-stage chain used across all EPW 2026 material. Used on the site to tag sessions.

stages.label: Scenarios and planning systems
stages.summary: Scenario governance, modelling tools, data, capacity, uncertainty and resilience — the planning systems that make long-term scenarios credible.

stages.label: Policy translation
stages.summary: Mandates, regulatory pathways, budgeting and coordination — how scenario insights become policies, roadmaps and decisions.

stages.label: Investment signals and pipelines
stages.summary: Planning information, sequencing, project preparation and risk allocation — the signals that turn a plan into an investable pipeline.

stages.label: Implementation and delivery
stages.summary: Procurement, markets, grids, system operation and institutional accountability — what it takes to deliver the plan on the ground.
